- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect risk reversal.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior period) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If model consistently underestimates in high-sentiment periods, apply a “mean reversion” bias: add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is positive and price has been trending down.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day trend if sentiment is stable or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.33), avoid large directional adjustments; use 1–2% smoothing to prevent overfitting to short-term noise.
